 Dated, this the 6th day of November, 2013
 Judgment

The petitioner in W.P.(C) No. 22160 of 2013 is running a shop dealing with sale of the product by name 'Panraj', while the petitioner in other case is the authorized State distributor of the very same commodity.

The grievance of the petitioners is common, in so far as the concerned respondents have seized the goods 'Panraj' from the shop of the petitioner in W.P.(C) No. 22160 of 2013 and others concerned, to whom the products were distributed by the petitioner in other case.

The seizure was with reference to the allegation that the article contains 'nicotine' or 'tobacco', which is a prohibited item.
2.
The case of the petitioners is that, the product being dealt with by the petitioners does not contain 'tobacco' or 'nicotine'.

Reliance is sought to be placed on Ext. P2 certificate issued by the manufacturer and also Ext. P3 certificate issued by a Government Laboratory, which clearly show that the product does not contain 'nicotine'.

The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that a Division Bench of this Court, vide Ext. P4 verdict dated 03.10.2012, W.P.(C) Nos. 22160 & 22438 of 2013 has held that, the enabling provisions to intercept and to proceed with further steps will be strictly subject to the presence of the ingredients of 'nicotine' or 'tobacco', so as to sustain the prohibition/ban of the product.

In view of the clearance given by the State Government Laboratory,
vide Ext. P3, as to the absence of 'nicotine' or 'tobacco' in the product 'Panraj', the whole exercise pursued by the respondents is per se wrong and illegal in all respects and hence the challenge.
3. A statement has been filed on behalf of the respondents, pointing out the actual facts and figures.
The relevant paragraphs (Paragraphs 2 and 3) are extracted below :

"2. It is submitted that the petitioner seeks interference of this Honourable Court mainly relying on Exhibit P4 judgment of this Honourable Court wherein it is clarified by the Division Bench of this Honourable Court that the Circular dated 22.05.2012 passed by this respondent only prohibits Gutka and Pan Masala containing Tobacco and Nocotine as ingredients by whatsoever name it is available in Ashraf K.I vs State Of Kerala on 3 October, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131227768/
3 the market.

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced Exhibit P2 certificate to the effect that the product Panraj does not contain Tobacco and Nicotine.

Further, Exhibit P3 Certificate W.P.(C) Nos. 22160 & 22438 of 2013 of Examination dated 5.11.2012 is also produced to substantiate the contention of the petitioner that the product Panraj does not contain Tobacco and Nicotine and therefore, conforms to the standard prescribed for Pan Masala under Regulation 2.11.2 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Product Standard and Food Additive) Regulation 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Product Standard and Food Additive) Regulation 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. In this connection, it is most respectfully submitted that the produce Panraj was initially seized from the various shops on the suspicion that the said product contained Nicotine or Tobacco, which is a prohibited item to be included in any food article as provided under Regulation 2.3.4. of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction of Sales) Regulation, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction of Sales) Regulation, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
After seizure of the product,
the same was sent for a detailed chemical examination by the Chief Food Safety Officer, Ernakulam to the Department of Health Service, Government Analyst's Laboratory, Kakkanad.

entities.text: Department of Health Service, Government Analyst's Laboratory, Kakkanad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The report of the Regional Analytical Laboratory dated 4.10.2013 shows that though the sample does not contain Nicotine or Tobacco, it contains Magnesium Carbonate, an anti caking agent, which is prohibited under Regulation 3.1.7 (1) of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Production Standard and Food Additive) Regulation 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Production Standard and Food Additive) Regulation 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, the product 'Panraj' is an 'unsafe food' coming under the definition of Section 3 (zz) (v) of Food Safety Standard Act 2006.

A true copy of the Report of the Food Analyst dated 04.10.2013 is produced herewith and marked as Annexure 1.
4.

The learned Government Pleader submits that Ext. P3 certificate issued form the concerned authority is in respect of a previous cause of action leading to search and seizure, whereas the present seizure has led to fresh examination of the sample for various items and as per Annexure A1 test report dated 04.10. 2013, the test conducted for ascertaining the presence of 'Carbonate' and Magnesium Carbonate has turned to be positive; though the test for 'nicotine' was found to be negative.

It is stated that 'Carbonate' and 'Magnesium Carbonate' (an anti caking agent) are prohibited items, and hence the sample does not conform to the standard prescribed for Pan masala falling under Regulation No. 2.11.5 of the Food Safety Standard (Food Product standard and Food Additive) Regulation 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety Standard (Food Product standard and Food Additive) Regulation 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As such, the product 'Panraj' is an 'unsafe food' coming under the definition of Section 3 (zz) (v) of Food Safety Standard Act 2006.
In view of the turn of events as above, the petitioners are liable to be W.P.(C) Nos. 22160 & 22438 of 2013 prosecuted by virtue of Section 59 of of the Act, submits the learned Government Pleader.

4. After hearing both the sides, this Court finds that there is no infringement of any provisions of law with regard to the seizure effected by the concerned respondent and that the proceedings are liable to be taken to a logical conclusion by way of prosecution proceedings, in view of the presence of the prohibited items 'Carbonate' and 'Magnesium Carbonate' in the product 'Panraj'.
In the said circumstances, interference is declined and both the writ petitions are dismissed.
This Court does not express anything with regard to the merit of the test reports.
